test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 12 Sept 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
The following diagram shows nutrition in amoeba. Which option correctly identifies the labelling 'a' and 'b' along with their functions?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2d5ab04b6249cdfbd14507121b570fa3ae0a4f012811916964b9085f41da428e.png]

options.text:
a - Pseudopodia (take in food)

b - Food vacuole (digestion of food)

a - Food vacuole (take in food)

b - Pseudopodia (absorption of food)

a - Food vacuole (absorption of food)

b - Food vacuole (digestion of food)

a - Pseudopodia (take in food)

b - Food vacuole (egestion of food)

solution:
The correct answer is __**option 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **a - Pseudopodia:** Pseudopodia are temporary, foot-like extensions of the cell membrane used by amoebas to move and capture food.
 
• **b - Food vacuole:** The food vacuole is an organelle where the digestion of ingested food particles occurs.
 
• **Function of Pseudopodia:** The pseudopodia extend and envelop food particles, effectively taking in food through a process called phagocytosis.
 
• **Function of Food Vacuole:** Once the food is enclosed in the food vacuole, digestive enzymes break down the food into simpler substances that can be absorbed by the cell.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pseudopodia:**

 
 
• Pseudopodia are also known as "false feet" and are characteristic of amoeboid cells.
 
• They help in locomotion and capturing prey through a process called phagocytosis.
 
• The formation of pseudopodia involves the flow of cytoplasm into the extension.
 
 
 
• **Food Vacuole:**
 
 
• The food vacuole is a membrane-bound organelle in amoeba where internal digestion occurs.
 
• After the pseudopodia capture food particles, these particles are enclosed in a food vacuole where digestive enzymes are secreted.
 
• These enzymes break down the food into simpler molecules that can be absorbed and utilized by the cell.
 
 
 
• **Phagocytosis:**
 
 
• Phagocytosis is the process by which a cell engulfs solid particles to form an internal compartment known as a phagosome.
 
• It is a crucial mechanism used by amoebas and certain immune cells to ingest foreign particles, including pathogens.
 
 
 
• **Digestion in Amoeba:**
 
 
• The digestion process in amoeba is intracellular, meaning it occurs within the cell.
 
• Once food is taken in through phagocytosis, it is enclosed in a food vacuole where digestive enzymes break down the food.
 
• The nutrients are then absorbed into the cytoplasm, and the waste is expelled from the cell.
